title: Passenger Door Structure — Hinge Lug and Web Crack Repair

ata.title: Passenger and Crew Doors — Door Structure

abstract: Repair of a crack in the passenger door hinge lug or in the adjacent web, by stop-drilling and strap where the crack is inside limits and by lug replacement where it is not.

sections.purpose: This repair restores a passenger door structure that has a crack in a hinge lug or in the web adjacent to it, without replacing the door.
sections.damage_assessment: A crack at a hinge lug is a load path finding, not a cosmetic one. Establish the crack length by dye penetrant before deciding anything; the visible length is usually shorter than the real one. Check the hinge and arm for wear at the same time, because a worn hinge puts the load into the lug in bending and the crack will come back if only the crack is repaired. Where the crack has crossed into the web, the lug replacement route applies regardless of length. Where two lugs on the same door show cracks, do not repair either: refer the door to engineering, because the two findings together point at a rigging problem rather than at the lugs.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Remove the door in accordance with the applicable maintenance task and support it on the door trestle. 2. Clean the area and do a dye penetrant inspection to establish the crack length and its ends. 3. Compare the crack length against the limits table. 4. Where the crack is inside limits and has not crossed into the web, stop-drill both ends to the diameter on the drawing and de-burr. 5. Install the strap D5210116303878 across the crack, using the gusset UMD412316-70 as backing where the drawing calls for it. 6. Where the crack has crossed into the web, remove the lug D5210122401685 and install the replacement lug D5210129309748 with the intercostal D5210122128111 as backing. 7. Do an eddy current inspection of every hole in the parent structure before any fastener is installed. 8. Install the fasteners wet with sealant and torque them in the marked sequence. 9. Restore the protective scheme. 10. Refit the door and rig it to the dimensions in the maintenance task. 11. Do a full door operation and locking test, and check the seal compression all round. 12. Record the repair position on the door repair map.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a dye penetrant inspection of the repaired area at installation and record the result with a photograph. Repeat the dye penetrant inspection of the stop-drilled crack ends every three thousand flight cycles for the life of the strap repair. Where the lug was replaced, do an eddy current inspection of the lug attachment row every six thousand flight cycles. At each inspection also check the hinge and arm wear; a repair that keeps cracking is a rigging finding and not a structural one.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Crack length up to 20 mm in the lug, not crossing into the web and not closer than 10 mm to a fastener hole. Only one repaired lug per door.

repair_drawings.title: Hinge lug strap and lug replacement details, passenger door structure

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of six, 18 mm pitch, 14 mm edge distance; fasteners installed wet with sealant
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The strap repair is life-limited to 12 000 flight cycles with a repeat dye penetrant inspection every 3 000 flight cycles. The lug replacement carries no life limit but requires an eddy current inspection of the attachment row every 6 000 flight cycles.
